Salaheddin Alzubi, Noah Provenzano, Jaydon Bingham, and colleagues let coding agents grow their own reusable skills. Their 2026 framework, EvoSkill, starts from a real gap: flexible agents still lack deep know-how for specialized tasks. Hand-written skill packs help, but they do not scale.

EvoSkill studies an agent's failures, proposes a new skill or an edit to an old one, and writes it as a structured folder. Only changes that improve held-out test scores survive, judged against a frontier of best programs, while the base model stays frozen. Gains appeared on two question-answering benchmarks over treasury and search tasks. Skills learned on one task even transferred to a fresh browsing benchmark, lifting scores with no changes.
arxiv-2603-03466:
Dinesh Parthasarathy and eleven colleagues discover that a DNA-organizing protein changes jobs when acidity rises. The Integration Host Factor compacts DNA inside bacteria by bending it, a well-understood role. Yet the same protein also scaffolds biofilms, the sticky bacterial communities, and bending alone could not explain that structural job. Biofilms are acidic inside, so their 2026 study varies acidity across the range found in biofilms.

Atom-level calculations showed low acidity reprograms the protein's chemistry, exposing positively charged patches on its surface. The team predicted those patches would let one protein bridge two separate DNA strands. Single-molecule and bulk experiments confirmed it: near normal acidity the protein mostly bends DNA, while in strong acidity it clearly crosslinks strands together. Acidity thus switches the protein's function, explaining how it mechanically supports biofilms.
arxiv-2603-03666:
Alexey Cheskidov and Hedong Hou prove that the equations of fluid motion can admit more than one future in rough function spaces. The Navier-Stokes equations govern viscous flow, and whether their mild solutions are unique is a basic question. Their 2026 paper shows unconditional uniqueness fails in every Besov space of negative regularity, the spaces rough enough to hold very singular data.

The counterexamples are striking: nontrivial stationary singular solutions, flows that sit still in time yet are genuinely rough, built through convex integration, a method that assembles wild solutions piece by piece. A counterweight result restores order at the boundary: stationary weak solutions are unique in an endpoint key space. The same conclusions extend to fractional Navier-Stokes equations with an arbitrarily strong smoothing operator, in both Lebesgue and Besov settings.
arxiv-2603-03766:
Hao Chang, Ruiying Hou, and Hui Wu classify the finite-size irreducible representations of certain modular super Yangians. Their subject is the Yangian associated with the general linear Lie superalgebra, defined over an algebraically closed field of prime characteristic greater than two. The paper treats two related algebras: the restricted super Yangian and the restricted truncated shifted super Yangian.

The result completes a representation-theoretic picture for these modular objects, which deform enveloping algebras and sit within quantum algebra. The work builds on the RTT presentation of Nazarov and the Drinfeld-type presentation developed by Gow, extending results of Drinfeld and of Brundan and Kleshchev. Such results organize which representations can occur and support further study of super Yangians in positive characteristic.
arxiv-2603-04166: Park and others learn hip exoskeleton control policy via predictive neuromusculoskeletal test. Their physics-based method trains hip-exoskeleton control wholly in test, with no motion-capture demonstrations, deploying it on hardware via policy distillation. On hardware, test-learned assistance profiles persist across matched speed-slope terms, giving quantitative sim-to-real transfer evidence without extra hardware tuning.
arxiv-2603-04566: Maurya and colleagues show flexible universal control in a planar trimon circuit. Multimode circuits offer flexible single and multi-qubit gates. The trimon integrates three transmon-like modes with strong ZZ links between every pair. Demonstrations include qubit rotations gated by one or by both partner qubits. They also include single qubit rotations that need no condition, plus two qubit entangling gates that keep or double excitations. Multi-tone driving implements all 16 two qubit Pauli operators, and as a qudit it reaches 8 levels with coherence above typical transmon devices.
arxiv-2603-04666: Daniels and colleagues derive the p-dissection of a product of quintuple products. Let p be a prime congruent to 1 mod 4, with p equal to m squared plus n squared, and let b be a positive integer. Q denotes the product in the quintuple product identity. The paper derives explicit formulas for the p-dissection of a product of two shifted Q values. It also determines sign patterns in length-p progressions of Taylor coefficients of the associated quotient. Combinatorial applications of the formulas are also given.
arxiv-2603-04866: Shuaichen Yan and colleagues propose Height Above Ellipsoid as one vertical reference for low-altitude airspace, replacing today's incompatible mix of barometric pressure, mean sea level, and height above ground. Their two-way conversion framework links the GNSS-native standard to legacy systems, tested in Shenzhen's divided airspace and in a risk study using PX4 flight logs. The switch shrinks required vertical separation while holding a target safety level, effectively opening more usable airspace.
arxiv-2603-05066: Michal Nauman and team present Reward-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning, an off-policy method that lets agents train under one nominal objective. They condition on varied reward parameterizations. Recomputing counterfactual rewards from shared replay data exposes the agent to several reward objectives without extra setting interaction, linking single-task RL with multi-objective and multi-task learning. On single-task, multi-task, and vision benchmarks, RCRL raises sample leanness under the nominal parameterization. It enables lean change to new ones and lets zero-shot behavioral change at deployment.
arxiv-2603-05466: Diez proves a free-probability version of Obata's rigidity theorem. In the old form, a sharp spectral gap forces a space to split off a 1D Gaussian factor. Under a non-commutative curvature-dimension rule, with Lipschitz conjugate variables, he shows that a non-zero saturator of the free Poincare inequality of Voiculescu must be affine in the generators. In short, the sharp case has one form. The von Neumann algebra must split off a freely complemented semicircular component, and the extremal directions form a free semicircular family.
arxiv-2603-05666: Spiesberger and team argue Ethereum needs fairness tools free of players' goodwill. Several tools hand block-content control to a proposer panel under a 1-of-n rule. Prior work shows roughly 91 percent of blocks are built by central firms taking user-adverse actions for gain, with proposers signing blindly and unable to step in. A common reading treats the left 9 percent as kind, but 2025 study finds at most 1.55 percent likely kind. Fairness tools relying on kind members would need larger panels than proposed, raising doubts it can work.
arxiv-2603-05766: Kataru and colleagues present a lock-free work-stealing queue. Work-stealing balances irregular workloads, and runtimes adopt lock-free deques. Existing algorithms target general runtimes and incur overheads. Their design supports bulk operations and assumes one owner and one stealer. An informal sketch shows the queue is linearizable and lock-free. Benchmarks show constant-latency push performance, stable as batch size increases. Pops perform comparably, while steal latency stays nearly flat across steal proportions. An optimized steal variant cuts latency by up to 3x.
arxiv-2603-06066: Kubesch and colleagues investigate open-weight language models for grading Austrian A-level German texts. Automated Essay Scoring has long aimed to support teachers by reducing workload and mitigating biases. A dataset of 101 anonymised exams across three text types was evaluated. Four models, DeepSeek, Qwen3, Mixtral, and LLama variants, were evaluated. The models reached a maximum of 40.6 percent agreement with the human rater, and under 33 percent of final grades matched experts. Results indicate that even though smaller models can use rubrics, they are not accurate enough for real-world grading.
arxiv-2603-06366: Fan and his team set out OralGPT-Plus, a vision language model for iterative symmetry aware reasoning on panoramic radiographs. Radiographs demand spatial work and bilateral understanding, while past models use a static single pass paradigm. DentalProbe, an expert curated five thousand image dataset with diagnostic paths, backs local inspection and other side comparison. Recheck driven reinforcement learning pushes rechecks while steadying long horizon thought through rubric based and test driven rewards. MMOral-X, with 300 open ended questions carrying region level notes, shows OralGPT-Plus beating strong baselines.
arxiv-2603-06566: Amsellem and colleagues present the first use of Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection for analyzing binary black hole mergers in the third gravitational-wave transient catalog. Paired with clustering, UMAP divides the population principally by primary and secondary mass components into four well-segregated subgroups, plus an outlier event. Objects near a 10 solar-mass buildup form their own group with aligned spins and low mass ratios. Objects at or above a 35 solar-mass overdensity form the largest group with lower effective spins and larger mass ratios.
arxiv-2603-06866: Xu and colleagues propose CAR, a framework for motion transfer to new vehicles via a shared motion code. Robot systems need platform data or simple models that miss motion physics across wheeled and tracked platforms, blocking scale-up. CAR encodes vehicle path changes and physical setups into a shared motion latent space with a Transformer encoder using adaptive normalization. Shared traits from nearest neighbors in that space enable fast switch to novel platforms with little data and compute, tested in the VertiBench simulator on the Chrono engine.
arxiv-2603-07366: Kharlamova and Proskurina tackle Russian first-language interference in English learner essays, where native habits leak into word choice and grammar. Their RILEC dataset pairs expert-annotated sentences with synthetic examples built by rule-based and neural augmentation. A generation framework using tuned language models plus prompt control and rules produces further motivated errors. Models trained on RILEC do well on word-level interference such as transliteration and tense meaning.
arxiv-2603-07566: Ferrari, Fraccaroli and Lamma propose GRD-Net for industrial surface anomaly detection with attention to regions of interest. Standard defect localization sets generated images against original ones, using blob analysis tuned to one dataset, and whole-image checks waste effort where anomalies do not matter. Their two-block design pairs a generative adversarial remaker with a masking block, trained on good products plus fake defects. Region-wise training teaches the network where anomalies count.
arxiv-2603-07666: Adrar and colleagues map phases in cycled sodium-ion cathode particles from X-ray spectral imaging with AI. Slow ion movement drives patchy phase births, mixed phases living together and uneven electric activity, complicating mechanism insight. Their workflow combines a Gaussian mixture variational coder with Pearson matching to map sodium content at nanometer detail within single grains. It reveals uneven phases and change, flagging doubt zones, false labels and boundary shifts.
arxiv-2603-07866: Almeida and colleagues build a language-guided grasping pipeline for a legged robot with an arm, meant for offshore inspection and upkeep. An operator names the target. The system finds it in colour images, builds a cloud of points from depth data, and fills gaps in sparse shape. It then picks a six-axis grasp that clears collisions and reach limits. In two cluttered tabletop trials drawn from small-object retrieval, it grasped far more often than a view-bound baseline.
arxiv-2603-07966: Zhou and colleagues study deictic commands in situated collaboration. The referent only becomes clear when speech lines up with a brief pointing stroke, so the task demands joint what, where, and when predictions. Many embodied benchmarks let language-only shortcuts succeed, so models score well without learning audio-visual alignment. Their EcoG-Bench offers 811 egocentric clips with annotations and millisecond-level stroke supervision in English and Chinese. Humans score near ceiling, while the best video-audio model reaches only about 17 percent, rising to about 43 percent with timestamped frames.
arxiv-2603-08066: Wei and colleagues report CGG-z7, the most compact galaxy group at redshift around 7, lying north of the GOODS-North field and observed by the JWST POPPIES program. At least six members fit a small projected area; four are confirmed spectroscopically through oxygen and hydrogen-beta emission. The group shows a low line-of-sight velocity dispersion against a substantial stellar mass, giving a stellar-to-dynamical mass ratio of 0.15 that exceeds typical values for virialized halos. That mix points to a group still assembling before virialization.
arxiv-2603-08166: Wang and colleagues present RexDrug, a reasoning-enhanced system for pulling multi-drug combinations from medical papers. Finding drug combinations in papers matters for precise treatment, but existing methods focus on binary interactions and struggle with variable-length n-ary sets, where compatibility rules are tangled and evidence is scattered. RexDrug trains in two stages. A multi-agent setup first writes expert-like reasoning traces for supervised tuning. Reinforcement learning with a rich reward then sharpens results and extraction accuracy.
arxiv-2603-08266: Basold and colleagues build a general theory of central limit results using dilated categories. The Central Limit Theorem states that large sequences of independent, identically spread random variables converge in probability to a normal curve, making it a basic building block of statistical thought. Yet no general theory of central-limit-type results exists, forcing workers to redo proofs without a grip on the key ingredients. The authors introduce dilated seminorm-enriched category theory as a unifying framework and prove an abstract central limit theorem within it.
arxiv-2603-08566: Andrew Chin and colleagues free seven contest cyber-reasoning systems for use on real open-source code. The contest systems were tied to cloud setups that no longer exist, leaving them idle outside their home teams. Their OSS-CRS frame runs and mixes the systems locally with budget-aware control, and porting the winning system turned up ten fresh bugs across eight fuzz projects.
arxiv-2603-08866: Rajintha Gunawardena and Fei He model phase-amplitude links as nonlinear motion, not filtered wiggles. Old methods read coupling off filtered phase and size traces, tripping on bandwidth, noise, and false echoes. Their ID frame finds a working model, runs it noise-free, and gauges coupling strength and preferred phase, staying sharp and robust in tests and rat brain recordings.
arxiv-2603-08966: Soares and colleagues derive the exact black hole solution in Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld gravity with perfect fluid dark matter. They trace how the event horizon and black hole size shift with the model parameters, probing the spacetime's core properties. Numerical study of massive-particle geodesics shows stable circular orbits react sharply to the system's coupling constants.
arxiv-2603-09166: Peaker Guo and colleagues make frequent-substring mining far cheaper while keeping differential privacy for each user's strings. A prior method reached near-optimal error but needed quadratic space and time. Their algorithm keeps the same error level yet cuts space and time close to linear in the input size. Two ideas drive the gain: smarter candidate generation from frequent prefixes and suffixes, plus pruning guided by frequency relations.
arxiv-2603-09466: Tony Danjun Wang and colleagues introduce TopoOR, a new way to represent the operating room that keeps group ties, not just pairwise ones. Surgical scene graphs flatten rich structure by passing messages between pairs or by token runs. TopoOR lifts interactions into higher-order topological cells, so pairwise and group relations survive along with their geometry. Its higher-order attention keeps each mode's features distinct across 3D geometry, audio, and robot kinematics, and the scheme includes classic scene graphs as a special case.
arxiv-2603-09666: Kazimierz Skrobas and colleagues present a method for reducing background in experimental spectra using the dual-tree complex wavelet transform. Fitting and filtering standards have limits, and Fourier-based techniques extract signals less well. Their algorithm works on arbitrary data ranges in time. It preserves the signal and cuts processing bias. It is demonstrated on X-ray powder diffraction and photoluminescence spectra of a beta gallium oxide crystal. Practical notes cover wavelet families and decomposition levels, and the method ships as a software package.
arxiv-2603-09766: Mithat Konuralp Demir documents a mentored study of Grassmann algebra and its invariant subalgebras, written in summer 2025. Opening sections set out the wedge product and build the algebra from a free associative one. A later section ties the exterior product closely to the determinant. The closing part gives what the author presents as a new classification of the invariant subalgebras.
arxiv-2603-09866: Helena Faustino Vieira and a large FEAST team give a first look at JWST spectra of young star clusters still emerging in galaxy NGC 628. The clusters sit in a bright complex in the northern spiral arm, wrapped in ionised gas and warm molecular material. Line strengths point to hot young massive stars as the main light source. Shocks from supernovae play little part, so early stellar feedback dominates here.
arxiv-2603-10066: Naimi writes a short note claiming that Stanfield's proof of Sachs' linkless embedding conjecture has a serious gap. The conjecture held that every linklessly embeddable graph also has a linear linkless embedding in three dimensional space. Naimi describes what he believes is the flaw in that proof. The note is brief and pointed, leaving the conjecture's status open again if his reading is right.
arxiv-2603-10166: Srikrishna Bangalore Raghu and coauthors release Dance2Hesitate, a multimodal data set of hesitant motion taught by dancers. A robot's hesitancy shapes how human partners coordinate, pay attention and judge safety, yet hesitant motion is hard to design across bodies and settings. The set pairs kinesthetic teaching on a Franka arm reaching toward a Jenga tower with dancer motion capture at three graded hesitancy levels. Whole body sequences for extreme hesitancy are included.
arxiv-2603-10566: E Callies and co-authors study the Rayleigh-Taylor instability in partly ionized plasmas, where ion-neutral coupling can bend the classic picture. They ran high-resolution two-fluid simulations across many wavelengths, coupling strengths, and magnetic setups. Linear growth rates matched theory from the single-fluid limit to mid coupling. In the nonlinear stage, ambipolar diffusion changes the growth law, and multi-wavelength runs turn strongly scale dependent, with fragmentation or smooth reorganization set by the coupling regime.
arxiv-2603-10666: Bert Jüttler, Pablo Mazón, and Josef Schicho classify, over the real numbers, the line congruences that arise from trilinear birational maps. Such maps show up in isogeometric analysis, and birational ones are valued because both map and inverse are rational and easy to evaluate. Their parameter lines form three families, which in the birational case fill space as congruences tied to rational maps. A complex-number classification existed already; this work gives the real counterpart, using line geometry.
arxiv-2603-10966: Pedro Ninhos and coauthors present a computational route to exciton physics in two-dimensional materials. It swaps the classical interaction models behind most fast calculations for quantum screened interactions. They work inside the Bethe-Salpeter equation, at the level of atoms. They compute the dielectric function at the random-phase approximation level. This reaches near first-principles quality at bearable cost. A full account of convergence settings also suggests why earlier binding energies from first-principles work scatter so widely.
arxiv-2603-11166: A. E. Watkins and coauthors test whether shape measurements from galaxy images can tell dwarf galaxies apart. The question matters because most dwarfs will be studied through broadband imaging alone. Common tests like concentration, asymmetry, and smoothness fail to discriminate dwarfs. Isophote-based options, twists, ellipticity, and profile residuals, prove as weak. Morphological classes blur, and no single statistical component explains much variance. Dwarf evolution from photometry alone will need high-dimensional population studies from surveys like the Legacy Survey of Space and Time.
arxiv-2603-11366: Lise Morlet-Decarnin, Thibaut Divoux, and Sébastien Manneville chart how suspensions of charged cellulose nanocrystals set into gels after a shear. These rod-like colloids are far less studied than spheres. Mechanical spectroscopy over time catches a sharp liquid-to-solid transition at a well-defined gel point. The spectra collapse onto master curves under a time-connectivity superposition. Varying crystal content and salt draws a boundary between gel and attractive glass. Critical exponents are asymmetric across the gel point and non-universal.
arxiv-2603-11466: Bagnara and co-authors prove that anomalous dissipation cannot occur for passive scalars under some random flows. The flows are autonomous and divergence-free, and they live on a torus. In two dimensions, the proof needs only almost sure continuity plus a mild nondegeneracy condition. In higher dimensions, it asks for a special geometric structure and Hölder exponent bigger than 1/8. No regularity is asked of the scalar itself, beyond bounded starting data. The same limits also block anomalous regularization, the Yaglom-Obukhov-Corrsin law, and Richardson diffusion.
arxiv-2603-12066: Vanga, Alatteili, and Iacocca probe resonance modes in a trilayer artificial spin ice. A square trilayer spin ice already shows rich behavior, and layers couple strongly here. Interfacial Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction makes the waves non-reciprocal inside the nanoislands. That shift remakes the standing wave modes that confined shapes support. Extra edge modes split in frequency as the interaction, applied field, and stray field interact. Their sign and strength also set whether those edge modes add or cancel.
arxiv-2603-12366: He, Khangaonkar, Pirsiavash, Bai, and Kolouri link drifting generative models to Sinkhorn divergence gradient flows. Drifting dynamics had left an identifiability gap: zero drift did not clearly force a match to the target. In a particle view, the drift splits into cross-minus-self parts via one-sided Gibbs kernels. Sinkhorn divergence shows the same split, but with two-sided scaling that enforces both marginals. Definiteness of that divergence then proves zero drift means the measures match. Experiments gain stability and far better one-step quality at low temperature settings.
arxiv-2603-13066: Alexander Gheorghiu defends the material conditional against the classic charge of paradox. Defined by truth values alone, it makes any conditional with a false start or true end come out true. Critics say such a connective cannot match plain if-then speech. He argues the clash comes from cognitive bias and misreading, not from meaning. The conditional belongs with indicative claims that track co-variation, not counterfactual ones. Read as marking entailment under a theory, it serves science well.
arxiv-2603-13666: Xiaofeng Liu and co-authors propose unsupervised adaptation from FDG to PSMA PET/CT for 3D lesion detection under label shift. Cross-tracer adaptation faces label shift in lesion size mix and lesions per subject. Their self-training framework models that shift with two mechanisms. Detection anchor shapes adapt from target pseudo labels by exponential moving average, raising coverage for small PSMA lesions. Size bin quotas for pseudo-label selection follow the estimated target histogram instead of a fixed threshold. On AutoPET 2024 the method beat baselines.
arxiv-2603-14066: Benac and co-authors build a benchmark for multi-party negotiation games drawn from real negotiation data. Real talks unfold as chains of binding, action-level pledges, not one final deal. Their setup pairs a configurable game generator with cases grounded in documents from a climate negotiation exercise. Several baseline solvers are included for comparison. No solver wins across all game types, since results hinge on each game's structure. The authors call for methods that value partial pledges more robustly.
arxiv-2603-14866: Li and Song blend statistical sampling with iterative regularization for sparse-view CT scans. Fewer views cut radiation dose but breed streak artifacts. Pure iterative fixes can spread errors and blur fine texture. Their hybrid model samples statistically while regularizing in steps. Sampling time shortens as image quality rises. Three test sets check the method. A Shepp-Logan phantom, real walnut X-ray data and clinical lung CT all serve. Detail and texture recovery improve over iterative baselines, they report.
arxiv-2603-14966: Henneking and co-authors forecast Cascadia tsunamis in real time from sparse offshore pressure data. A test network of 175 ocean-bottom sensors feeds the system. Bayesian inversion recovers the seafloor velocity field as waves evolve. Acoustic and tsunami wavefields match for two minutes, then split apart. That split lets the system tell rupture scenarios apart fast. Precomputed physics splits work between a big offline phase and a laptop online phase. Wave height forecasts land in under a second. Errors stay near twenty percent in both rupture cases.
arxiv-2603-15266: Peron and co-authors review Galactic cosmic rays and ask what future MeV detectors could reveal about them. Low-energy cosmic rays matter most for ionization, outflows, and star and planet formation. The review covers direct measurements, acceleration models, and propagation through the Galactic disk. It then surveys the current state of gamma-ray observations, a key window on cosmic ray interactions. The authors close with prospects for new MeV missions to probe the physical traits of these particles.
arxiv-2603-15366: Dehne introduces the RIGHT framework for judging the validity of research software aimed at human users. Quality work in research software has stressed reliability and the FAIR principles, leaving validity thinly covered. RIGHT grows out of theory transfer and process modeling. It draws on models from simulation research, design-based research, software engineering, and social science. Two case studies from learning technologies show how the framework applies in practice. The target is research integrity for human-facing tools.
arxiv-2603-15566: Stetsenko proposes Lore, a protocol that turns git commit messages into structured decision records for AI coding agents. Each commit keeps the code change but drops the reasoning behind it, a loss he calls the Decision Shadow. Lore uses native git trailers to store constraints, rejected options, agent directives, and check results inside the message. It needs no new infrastructure and ships with a query tool any shell-capable agent can run. The paper formalizes the scheme, weighs five rival approaches, and maps a validation path.
arxiv-2603-15766: Farag and co-authors run Cepheid star pulsations inside a full evolution code. Stellar modelers usually split evolution and pulsation into separate workflows. The team adds eddy-viscous damping to MESA's time-dependent convection treatment. The change aligns MESA-TDC with the MESA-RSP pulsation module. A 6 solar-mass blue-loop model then evolves through large pulsations in one run. Periods, light curves, and growth rates match a paired RSP run well. Coupled runs now support studies with rotation and mass loss.
arxiv-2603-15966: Godinho and Murphy extend surface dissections and build piano algebras from them. Admissible dissections cut marked surfaces into simple pieces. Their extended version widens that older notion. Each dissection yields a differential graded algebra, the piano algebra. Piano algebras act as graded cousins of gentle algebras. For a plain marked disc, the algebra matches a known endomorphism ring. That ring generates a completed discrete cluster category of type A. Two piano algebras from matching discs prove derived equivalent.
arxiv-2603-16366: Nöhre and co-authors draw concept lattices with a force-directed method called DimFlux. Concept lattices are central objects in formal concept analysis. Force methods treat a diagram as a physical model under forces. Earlier work covered only attribute-additive diagrams. DimFlux lets both attributes and objects set node positions. A DimDraw start replaces the older planarity enhancer. The goal is wider spacing between nodes and stray edges, for readability.
arxiv-2603-16466: Koshi and co-authors compare light curves across Type Ia supernova subclasses. The Branch system sorts these explosions into four groups. Prior work focused near peak brightness, leaving late times unclear. The team built average light curves for 109 events. Curves run from before maximum into the late tail. The I-band shows the strongest diversity between groups. Secondary maximum timing tracks the stable iron share. Cool events fade with a distinct late slope, a handy diagnostic.
arxiv-2603-16666: Yuan and co-authors ask if robot world models must imagine the future at test time. World action models foresee how scenes change under actions. Most versions imagine, then execute, which costs time. Their Fast-WAM keeps video co-training but skips test-time prediction. Variants split the two factors for a clean comparison. Dropping imagination barely hurt performance. Dropping video training hurt far more. Fast-WAM runs at 190 ms latency, over four times faster. Video's value lies in training, they conclude.
arxiv-2603-16966: Huang and co-authors present CineSRD, a system that labels who speaks when in films and TV shows. Classic diarization targets meetings and interviews, with few speakers and clean sound. Visual media add long videos, many speakers, mismatched audio and visual cues, and wild conditions. CineSRD uses visual, acoustic, and linguistic cues from video, speech, and subtitles. It first clusters visual anchors to register speakers. An audio language model then detects speaker turns and adds off screen voices. The team also releases a benchmark covering Chinese and English programs.
arxiv-2603-17166: Carron and Reinecke describe a fast algorithm for partial sky spherical harmonic transforms. Such transforms are a workhorse of cosmic microwave background analysis. Their method builds on the Fourier sphere approach and handles many arbitrary locations on the sphere well. The driving uses are CMB lensing with the South Pole Telescope and the hunt for primordial gravitational waves. On test fields, they report speed ups of 3 to 10 times, and much more on smaller patches. They argue the method removes the usual drawbacks of arbitrary pixelisations.
arxiv-2603-17766: Zavorka and co-authors measure vehicle-to-vehicle radio channels at 60 and 80 gigahertz. Two cars drove toward each other while a time-domain sounder logged the channel. Power delay profiles track how multipath parts evolve during the pass. Delay spread at 60 gigahertz looks Gaussian with a higher median, they report. At 80 gigahertz it turns lognormal with a lower median. Resolvable paths run nearly twice as many at 60 gigahertz.
arxiv-2603-18066: Oh presents a synthesizable RTL design that runs predictive coding networks directly in hardware. Backpropagation needs global error flow and central memory, which block online, spread-out learning. Each core here holds its own activity, prediction error, and weights. Cores talk only to adjacent layers through hardwired links. A uniform clamping step sets boundary conditions for both learning and inference, with a fixed finite-state schedule.
arxiv-2603-18266: Ranjan and co-authors present Enactor, a transformer world model that turns traffic simulators into surrogate models. Standard microsimulators use simple behavior rules and miss real actor interactions. Learned agent models capture interaction but drift over long horizons and at intersections. Enactor learns actor interactions plus intersection geometry for grounded trajectories. In a SUMO-in-the-loop test over 40,000 steps, it beat the baseline by over tenfold on KL divergence.
arxiv-2603-18366: Zhao and co-authors boost vacuum-ultraviolet dispersive-wave emission with gas-filled tapered hollow-core fibers. Laser work on the thorium-229 nuclear transition needs bright sources near 148.38 nanometers. Standard fibers trade off input coupling against conversion intensity by core size. A tapered core joins a large input opening with steady field concentration along its length. The source tunes from 135 to 240 nanometers and doubles efficiency at the thorium line.
arxiv-2603-18566: Liu builds dark matter and the strong CP problem into one type IIA string theory setup. The model uses intersecting D6-branes on an orientifold and gives a three-generation spectrum like the MSSM. Moduli are fixed through the STU model and the KL mechanism. Dark matter then has two parts: axions and the neutralino. A four-form flux mechanism is added to address the strong CP problem. Liu computes relic amounts and discusses what observers could detect.
arxiv-2603-18666: Xu and co-authors build a parametric amplifier inside a double quantum dot circuit. Such amplifiers are key for high-fidelity qubit readout but suffer loss and weak tuning. Their design uses the dot's own nonlinearity inside a superconducting cavity with two gallium arsenide dots. Gain passes 11 decibels. Reading out a second dot with this amplifier more than doubles the signal-to-noise ratio. The device also resists magnetic fields better than standard options. The team presents it as a flexible platform for microwave quantum circuits.
arxiv-2603-19066: Liu and co-authors test a classic shape theory of word analogy with help from language models. The theory says an analogy forms a parallelogram in word vector space. Past work found people often stray from that shape. The team compares human and model completions on the same problem set. Model answers are judged better than human ones and sit closer to the parallelogram form. The gain comes from shape alignment, not from picking nearby words. Tuning word vectors toward the shape also boosts prediction of human ratings.
arxiv-2603-19466: Min and co-authors test whether multimodal models know when to ask a user for help. A person facing a blocked object would ask for the block to move. Their ProactiveBench reworks seven data sets into tasks that reward such requests. Tasks span hidden objects, poor image quality, and rough sketches. All 22 tested models show weak proactive behavior overall. Bigger models do no better, and hints add only small gains. Chat history and in-context examples can even hurt scores. A light reinforcement tuning step does teach the skill.
arxiv-2603-19666: S and co-authors study the fault-tolerant metric dimension of subdivided zero divisor graphs. The base graph links non-zero zero-divisors of a ring, joined when their product is zero. Subdivision inserts a new vertex on each edge. The team works with integers modulo n, where n is a product of two distinct odd primes. They find the fault-tolerant metric basis for this graph. They also prove a lower bound of q minus one on its dimension, with q the larger prime.
arxiv-2603-19766: Fang and co-authors adapt a single-cell foundation model to predict spatial gene expression. Their target is expression maps inferred from stained tissue images. Spatial transcriptomics gives such maps, but it is costly and slow. Pure image generators often ignore links between genes. The base model already knows many of those links. Their HINGE system adds a light visual pathway to that model. A masked diffusion goal keeps training aligned. On three datasets it beat prior methods on correlation and marker patterns.
arxiv-2603-20366: Zhang and co-authors present WebNavigator, a system for global navigation of the web by AI agents. Agents today wander by trial and error, lacking a map of the site. The authors call this flaw topological blindness. WebNavigator builds interaction graphs offline at zero token cost. Online, it retrieves a route, reasons over it, and teleports along it. On WebArena multi-site tasks, it reached a 72.9% success rate. That score more than doubled enterprise-level agent results.
arxiv-2603-20466: Kocabay and Akkuş present Diffutron, a masked diffusion language model built for Turkish. Turkish has rich word forms, and few models of this type target it. Their training path starts with LoRA based pre-training of a multilingual encoder. A staged instruction tuning plan then adds text generation skills. The model stays small next to rival systems with billions of parameters. Yet tests across many benchmarks show it performs on par with them. The work backs masked diffusion as a path for Turkish text.
arxiv-2603-20566: Kanwal and co-authors model a suspension bridge deck as a nonlinear plate. The model adds fractional damping and a memory term with no time limit. A source term can also drive the system toward failure. They first prove local well posedness in an energy space. They then give terms for global solutions with fast decay. If the start energy is negative, solutions blow up in finite time. A numeric scheme built on SBP-SAT and Newmark steps matches both regimes.
arxiv-2603-20666: Tatematsu and co-authors map deuterated molecules in the Orion molecular clouds. They use the Nobeyama 45 meter radio telescope with a new receiver. Their targets are a bent filament and twenty starless cores in Orion A and B. DNC spread across the whole filament they mapped. DCO+ stayed local, near the OMC-3 region. Ratios of DNC to its normal form ran high in OMC-2 and OMC-3. Inside single cores the ratios held near constant, though cores differ from each other.
arxiv-2603-20866: Dey studies entanglement between two qubits that share one cavity. The work follows an earlier study where the cavity started empty. Here the cavity starts with some excitations present. Dey also lets the two qubits couple to the cavity with unequal strength. In a closed system, past a set ratio of couplings no fully entangled state can form. That threshold depends on how full the cavity starts. In a driven, lossy setup, steady entanglement varies in a non simple way with drive strength.
arxiv-2603-20966: Al Daas and co-authors set communication lower bounds for sketching with random dense matrices. Sketching supports low rank approximation and column subset selection, and is widely used in machine learning. On distributed machines, moving data is often the main cost, yet parallel sketching was little studied. They prove how much data movement any parallel method needs. They give algorithms that meet the bounds, and extend the results to Nyström approximation. Their code scales well on modern CPU and GPU clusters.
arxiv-2603-21066: Crespo-Rodriguez and co-authors study how road features and vehicle dynamics jointly shape self-driving test outcomes. Simulation testing is cheaper than field testing, but the scenario space is vast. Past work treated static road features and dynamic vehicle behavior apart. They use Instance Space Analysis to study both together. Models trained on both feature types predict test outcomes better than models trained on one type. The interplay also improves fault detection. Their frame supports outcome prediction without running each test, which helps regression testing.
arxiv-2603-21166: Xia and Liu present a training-free system that rebuilds 3D indoor scenes from a few unposed photos. Radiance field methods need dense views and per-scene optimization. Their pipeline needs neither training nor pose preprocessing. A warping based filter removes unreliable geometry from the point cloud. Segmentation masks from 2D images are lifted into a consistent, instance aware 3D form. New views are rendered from the point cloud, then refined by a 3D-aware diffusion model. Object removal edits follow from point cloud changes alone, with no retraining.
arxiv-2603-21266: Kumar and co-authors design a low-cost datalogger for indoor and outdoor air quality monitoring. Demand for cheap monitors grows as public and research interest rises. Their device runs on solar power, batteries, or direct supply, with a built-in battery charger. It links through WiFi, Bluetooth, and LoRaWAN. Users can swap the microcontroller unit to match connectivity, power, and compute needs. The design stresses low power use while data integrity is kept.
arxiv-2603-21366: Zhao and co-authors introduce Relax Forcing, a memory mechanism for long autoregressive video generation. Forcing based training reduces exposure bias, but minute scale videos still degrade over time. Their analysis shows that keeping more past frames does not always help. Relax Forcing splits temporal context into three roles: sink frames for global stability, tail frames for short term continuity, and selected history frames for mid-range motion. On VBench-Long, it improves motion dynamics and overall scores over autoregressive baselines.
arxiv-2603-21466: Lee and co-authors build GateANN, a system for filtered vector search stored on SSDs. Existing systems either waste disk reads by filtering after retrieval or need costly index rebuilds. GateANN instead splits graph traversal from vector retrieval. It checks each node's filter in memory first, and routes through non-matching nodes without any disk read. Matching nodes are fetched only when needed. In experiments, GateANN cut SSD reads by up to ten times and raised throughput by up to 7.6 times.
arxiv-2603-21566: Eslami and co-authors present CataractSAM-2, a model that segments cataract surgery video in real time. It adapts Meta's Segment Anything Model 2 to eye surgery. Live, accurate masks matter for robot-aided and computer-guided surgery. The team also built a labeling tool that pairs sparse prompts with video mask propagation. That tool cuts labeling time and helps build ground-truth sets at scale. The model also worked on glaucoma trabeculectomy video with no retraining, they report.
arxiv-2603-21966: Aung and co-authors release BHDD, a dataset of handwritten Burmese digits for machine learning practice and research. The set holds 87,561 grayscale images in the 28 by 28 MNIST format, split into ten classes. Training uses 60,000 images balanced across classes, while the test set keeps the natural class frequencies from collection. Over 150 writers of varied ages and backgrounds took part. The team studies class balance, pixel statistics, and shape variation, and flags digit pairs confused by the script's round forms. Three simple baseline models score between 99.4 and 99.8 percent.
arxiv-2603-22066: Teles and co-authors comment on a 2023 study of phase transitions in a mean field model. That study used linear stability analysis of the Vlasov equation to locate the transition. Teles and his team run molecular dynamics simulations with 100 million particles instead. They find the flagged threshold is not a ferromagnetic transition at all. The system stays paramagnetic there, its magnetization averaging to zero. The true transition comes at much stronger coupling and is discontinuous. They conclude bifurcation analysis cannot predict the long-time fate of such systems.
arxiv-2603-22166: Eskandarlou and co-authors test how well the J-PAS survey can read the stars in faint tidal features. Galaxies that merge leave diffuse trails of stars behind. Spectra of those trails need very long exposures. J-PAS instead uses 54 narrow-band filters over a wide sky area. The team studies one late-stage merger, PGC 3087775, in early J-PAS data. J-PAS points to a less metal-rich mix with a faster star formation history than SDSS suggests. It also sharpens stellar mass estimates fourfold.
arxiv-2603-22266: Moon reviews how scientists now probe the properties of liquids at the atomic scale. Liquids lack the fixed structure of solids, and their atoms keep moving. That disorder long blocked strict microscopic theories of liquid behavior. New computing power and better instruments have changed the picture. Moon covers theory and simulation tools such as instantaneous normal modes and velocity autocorrelation functions. On the lab side, he focuses on X-ray and neutron scattering. He closes with open chances and next steps for the field.
arxiv-2603-22566: Pessianzadeh and co-authors analyze how abortion access barriers surface in Reddit posts after the Dobbs ruling. The 2022 decision reshaped United States abortion law and access. The team studies over seventeen thousand posts from four related forums. They sort posts by information type, stage, barrier kind, and emotion. Eight barrier types frame the coding, from legal and money hurdles to social pressure. Emotional and psychological barriers dominate the stories throughout. Feelings like fear, confusion, and sadness run through posts at every stage.
arxiv-2603-22766: Parmar and Silpasuwanchai study human-AI negotiation over many issues at once. They built a rental negotiation case and varied the issue count. Without support, performance holds up to three issues, then drops as mental load grows. Their aid is a visualization driven by Bayesian estimates of agreement chance. It shows the space of shared acceptable deals shrinking over time. In a test with 32 people, the aid improved outcomes and speed. It also kept human control and did not shift value unfairly.
arxiv-2603-23066: Matteucci reviews the time-delay model and its uses in galactic archaeology. The model reads abundance diagrams that plot element ratios against iron content. Its base is stellar lifetimes: stars of distinct masses make distinct elements on distinct clocks. Alpha elements arrive fast from massive stars. Most iron arrives late, from Type Ia supernovae in binary systems. That delay explains the high alpha share at low metallicity. Matteucci shows how the model constrains star formation histories. Uses cover the Milky Way, other galaxy types, and high-redshift objects.
arxiv-2603-23166: Ren and Winterhof compare two ways to judge how random a binary sequence looks. Each way comes in a plain form and a symmetric form, which reads the sequence in reverse as well. For sequences built from prime expansions, the symmetric 2-adic score can be strictly lower than the plain one. For the linear score, reversal changes nothing, they reprove. For finite sequences, both symmetric scores can fall well below the plain ones. The gap in expected values grows with sequence length, they show.
arxiv-2603-23266: Schütte and three co-authors solve a gap between cheap coarse models and full dynamics. Motion is often simulated on a few collective variables, which is fast but coarse. Turning a coarse path back into full atom-level paths is the hard part. Their method guides full-system runs to track the coarse path. A Girsanov reweighting then removes the bias from that guidance. Tests show coarse paths become realistic full paths with barrier crossings and detours. The weighted ensembles also speed up path statistics.
arxiv-2603-23366: Manuilov extends continuous fields of C-star algebras to Hilbert C-star bimodules. He starts with a poset carrying a growing family of ternary rings of operators. He equips the poset with a zero-dimensional Hausdorff topology and a compactification. That space becomes the base for a field of bimodules. His example uses coarse equivalence classes of metrics on two spaces. Each class yields a Roe bimodule linking the two Roe algebras. The family grows with the order, so the field arises on its own.
arxiv-2603-23466: Liang and Head-Gordon chase the accuracy ceiling of hybrid density functional theory for molecules. Working functionals must trade simplicity, accuracy, and transfer across tasks. The pair set a strict protocol that mixes firm constraints, flexible forms, and modern fitting. Applied to range-separated hybrid meta-GGA forms, it yields the COACH functional. On broad molecular benchmarks, COACH beats leading rivals like omegaB97M-V on both counts. It keeps the same rung's low cost. Their trade-off study hints that real gains now need nonlocal input.
arxiv-2603-24566: Kiss and co-authors build a safety-critical control framework for nonlinear systems with input delay. Delays make controllers react late and too strongly, risking unsafe states and infeasible inputs. Their approach builds on integral control barrier functions and embeds predictor feedback into a dynamic control law, so the predicted state follows delay-free dynamics. A quadratic program then designs the safe control. For systems with both state and input constraints, they derive a closed-form feasibility condition. Robust variants handle prediction errors from delay uncertainty, using tunable barrier functions.
arxiv-2603-24666: Grassi and co-authors bound the Mordell-Weil rank of elliptic fibrations. They prove the Mordell-Weil group of such a fibration embeds into that of a suitable elliptic surface. Conditions for those surfaces to exist are given. Applying it yields explicit rank bounds for elliptic threefolds of Kodaira dimension zero, including Calabi-Yau threefolds. New explicit bounds follow for a broad class of elliptic fourfolds. The results suggest a general linear rank bound, stated as a conjecture.
arxiv-2603-24766: Wang and co-authors calculate electrodynamic signatures of Bogoliubov Fermi surfaces in moiré graphene. Superfluid stiffness mixes two parts, complicating its link with tunnelling data. Tunnelling data showing V-to-U shape changes and finite zero-bias conductance have hinted at such a Fermi surface, often tied to pair-density-wave order. The authors compute the stiffness under that pairing state. Virtual interband processes supply the geometric part that keeps the condensate rigid. Gapless quasiparticles on the Fermi surface can respond to a phase gradient through the pair structure.
arxiv-2603-24866: Yang and co-authors present DreamHouse, a benchmark for physical generative reasoning in vision-language models. Most benchmarks reward visually plausible output, not whether a model grasps the steps needed to build it. DreamHouse asks for artifacts meeting geometric, structural, constructability, and code-compliance constraints at once. The domain is home timber-frame construction, with codified standards and correctness checks. Over 26,000 structures in 13 styles are verified to construction-document level. A ten-test scoring framework rates the builds, and models can iterate against mid-build states.
arxiv-2603-25066: Qi, Earls, and Peng build a foundation model that learns quantum motion itself, not just one run of it. Older tools must restart for each new drive pattern. Their Neural Operator Quantum State learns the map from a drive protocol to the states it produces. Once trained, it predicts new ones in one pass. Tests use the 2D Ising model with shifting fields. The model stays accurate on new drive shapes, even ones unlike its training set. It also moves across time grids and fine-tunes on sparse data.
arxiv-2603-25266: Zhang and Wiklicky bring probabilistic abstract interpretation to neural networks. The method reasons about all inputs at once when testing each one is out of reach. Instead of single outputs, it tracks how input density flows through the network. The pair shows how the framework maps onto networks. They discuss abstract domains, the pseudo-inverses each one needs, and the transformers that move densities between layers. Small worked examples show how the analysis answers real questions about a network's behavior.
arxiv-2603-25366: Castelo-Branco, Santos-Victor, and Bernardino mix Bayesian belief maps with learned control so a robot can hunt for objects indoors. The robot never sees the whole room, and its sensors are unsure. A belief map tracks where the target likely sits, updated by Bayes' rule from calibrated detections. A reinforcement policy then picks moves straight from that map. In Habitat 3.0 tests across two indoor scenes, the hybrid finds objects more often and with less search effort than baseline plans.
arxiv-2603-25566: Qi and co-authors judge re-encoded user videos by how they look, not by how close they sit to a flawed source. Home clips arrive pre-damaged by edits and past compression. A codec that copies the source copies its scars too. Their Mamba-based quality model learns from weak ranking signals in a Siamese setup. Plugged into two neural codecs as the loss, it steers rebuilds toward cleaner looks. Bit rate savings reach about eight and thirteen percent against two strong codec families.
arxiv-2603-25666: Mannella, Di Carlo, and Savino test how well FreeRTOS holds up when faults strike its kernel. They built KRONOS, a tool that injects faults into kernel data structures from software. It needs no special hardware or debug ports. Their campaign targets scheduler variables and task control blocks. They track effects on correctness, timing, and availability. The authors report that damage to pointers and key scheduler variables often causes crashes. Many task control block fields, by contrast, have only a small effect.
arxiv-2603-25766: Wang and co-authors present ETA-VLA, a way to cut the cost of vision-language-action models for driving. Such models read past frames from many cameras, which makes self-attention very costly. ETA-VLA adds an aggregator inside the language model that prunes visual tokens. A text-guided score and a diversity rule keep only the key tokens. On the NAVSIM v2 benchmark, the authors report driving scores near the best baselines. The method prunes 85 percent of visual tokens. It keeps 94 percent of the original accuracy.
arxiv-2603-26066: Cheng, Hatano, and Takimoto study adversarial bandit problems where losses are bent versions of linear ones. Each round, the learner picks an action and then sees a loss. The loss is a linear part plus a perturbation chosen by an adversary. A global budget caps the total size of all perturbations. The authors prove expected and high-probability regret bounds for this model. As a side result, they improve the classic bound for bandit linear optimization. They also prove a matching lower bound on expected regret.
arxiv-2603-26166: Vila, Saulo, and Quintino build a family of inequality measures that joins two classics. The Hoover index and the Gini coefficient sit at the two ends. Their measure blends deviations from the mean with pairwise differences in one convex mix. The blend keeps scale invariance, boundedness, and the Pigou-Dalton transfer rule. Closed forms exist for gamma distributions. The authors derive the plug-in estimator's bias in closed form. Simulations show the bias shrinks as samples grow.
arxiv-2603-26266: Xie and co-authors present GUIDE, a plug-in that helps GUI agents handle software they were not trained on. Agents often lack the workflows and layouts of niche apps, which the team calls domain bias. GUIDE pulls how-to videos from the web and mines their subtitles in three steps to find ones that fit the task. An automated pipeline then infers plan and grounding facts from key frames. Tests on OSWorld lift success by over 5% with no model changes.
arxiv-2603-26966: Azevedo and Boschi-Filho connect a classical vibrating drumhead to the masses of glueballs. Glueballs are particles made only of gluons, the carriers of the strong force. Holographic quantum chromodynamics predicts their masses through a hardwall model. The model's differential equations turn out to match those of a circular membrane. A drumhead's vibration modes thus mirror the glueball spectrum calculation. The authors present this overlap as extra motivation for undergraduates. Studying membrane dynamics then doubles as a route into holographic methods.
arxiv-2603-27266: Mehta studies multiple zeta functions and their variants at identical arguments. Through the harmonic product, these functions become polynomials in the Riemann zeta function. Their coefficients take an explicit form via complete Bell polynomials. That form makes the functions' singularities easy to read off. It also yields a functional relation linking several families at once. The multiple zeta, multiple t, and star variants are tied together this way. At equal arguments, that corner case becomes fully explicit here.
arxiv-2603-27466: Frobenius and Stickelberger appear here in a fresh English translation. Their short 1877 paper treats elliptic functions. It first ran in Crelle's journal in German. The main result is a determinant formula for elliptic functions. That formula now bears both authors' names. It extends older determinant results by Hermite and Kiepert. The translation makes a classic source open to new readers. It also preserves the paper in digital form.
arxiv-2603-27766: Dürr lets a coding agent improve Bayesian models on its own. AutoStan loops through write, sample, judge, and revert steps. Stan model files are edited by a command-line agent. Held-out predictive scores guide each keep-or-drop call. Sampler warnings add a second feedback channel. On outlier data, the agent finds robust t-based forms. It matches a top black-box method while staying readable. Four more tasks yield hierarchical and sports models.
arxiv-2603-27866: Liu and co-authors train video models to reason with checkable rewards. Video generators look smooth but plan poorly. Group relative policy optimization adapts to flow-based models. Maze solving and robot navigation serve as tasks. Multimodal reward models fail badly in this setting. Hand-built verifiable rewards ground training in true metrics. Maze exact match rises 29.1 percent over supervised tuning. Trap avoidance jumps 51.4 percent.
arxiv-2603-27966: The Euclid Collaboration tests how well theory predicts the galaxy power spectrum and bispectrum for the Euclid space mission. The team uses mock catalogues of hydrogen-alpha galaxies drawn from the Flagship I simulation. One-loop and tree-level models give unbiased results up to set scale limits in real and redshift space. Adding the bispectrum to the power spectrum tightens key constraints by up to 30% and roughly doubles the figure of merit.
arxiv-2603-28066: Chen and Kumar propose Synonymix, a way to simulate groups rather than single people or whole populations. Their pipeline merges many life-story personas into one graph, called a unigraph, that keeps ties to real experience. Users can explore this group portrait or sample fresh synthetic personas from it. On General Social Survey items, the synthetic agents kept real behavior signals well past demographic baselines. Each source story also adds under 13% of any output, a privacy guard.
arxiv-2603-28166: Zhang and seven co-authors test how safely AI agents use real-world tools and the privileges that come with them. GrantBox, their sandbox, plugs in genuine tools and lets agents call real privileges under prompt injection attacks. Agents showed basic caution and blocked some direct attacks. Cleverer attacks still succeeded 84.8% of the time on average in crafted scenarios. The findings show privilege control is a weak point in current agent design.
arxiv-2603-28566: Lamata-Otín and co-authors ask how changing group membership shapes contagion in higher-order systems. Group reinforcement can cause sudden jumps from inactive to active phases. Past work often used static groups or mean-field shortcuts. Their model uses a turnover rate to bridge fixed and mean-field limits. They find that turnover can broaden the bistable region and help or hinder spread near the threshold. With real turnover rates and varied group sizes, four distinct phases appear.
arxiv-2603-28666: Xu proposes that changing-look active galactic nuclei arise from changes in the inner ADAF disk size. The accretion disk has an outer thin part and an inner thick ADAF part. The ADAF size is unstable and evolves over time. A turbulence parameter sets the ADAF size and the accretion rate. It also controls jet formation, outflow, and line-of-sight absorption. Changing-state and changing-observation nuclei then become two sides of one coin. Xu also links large ADAFs to some compact radio sources.
arxiv-2603-29066: Garba and Volonakis study energy level alignment in vacancy-ordered halide double perovskites. These lead free compounds are stable and tunable for optoelectronics. Using a dielectric dependent hybrid functional, they study Cs2MX6 compounds with varied metals and halogen types. Bulk band gaps agree well with GW results, which validates the approach. Surface stability depends on chemical potential, with CsX terminations favored. MX4 terminations show in-gap states that can trap carriers. From absolute energy levels, they name strong candidates for charge transport layers.
arxiv-2603-29366: Awan and Raza test if language models can write prior authorization letters. These letters ask insurers to approve care in advance. The task eats billions of dollars and many doctor hours each year. They scored three commercial models on 45 checked cases. The cases spanned five fields of medicine. All three models wrote strong clinical content. Their diagnoses and medical need claims were sound. A second check found gaps in admin details. Billing codes, time spans, and follow-up plans were often missing.
arxiv-2603-29466: Grünefeld and co-authors give a cheap way to gauge neural network doubt. Exact methods cost too much for large models. Their trick uses two shortcuts. First, a Taylor step ties the doubt to the slope of the output. Second, they treat weight spread as equal in all directions. One pass yields the model-doubt part from a gradient norm. The data-noise part comes from the prediction itself. Checks against costly sampling matched well. On quiz tests, the signal helped on TruthfulQA but not TriviaQA.
arxiv-2603-29566: Hendi and co-authors study the geometry of polynomial group convolutional neural networks. These networks work for any finite group. Their framework uses graded group algebras to describe the design. Two natural parameter forms appear, based on Hadamard and Kronecker products. A linear map ties the two forms together. They compute the size of the neuromanifold for the network. It depends only on layer count and group size. Both parameter maps turn out to be identifiable, up to symmetry and scaling.
arxiv-2603-29866: Berger and co-authors test a new way to pair human and AI judgments. The usual setup has AI advise and a human accept or reject. People often ignore good advice and swallow bad advice. Their hybrid confirmation tree instead collects both judgments independently. Agreement settles the call, and a second human breaks ties. Across ten datasets, the tree beats the advisor setup every time. It also wins when the AI explains itself.
arxiv-2604-00066: Martínez and five colleagues compare evolution strategies with deep reinforcement learning across game and robot-control tasks, asking whether the simpler, derivative-free method can serve as useful pretraining. Their tests show evolution strategies do not reliably train faster, and as a warm-up they help only on the simplest task, Flappy Bird. On Breakout and MuJoCo Walker they add little or nothing to training speed or stability across settings.
arxiv-2604-00166: Murgui presents a high-energy Standard Model completion unifying quarks and leptons under color SU(4). One real antisymmetric fermionic representation tackles the strong CP problem via Nelson-Barr, and repairs Pati-Salam mass links between charged leptons and down quarks for the two heaviest generations. Phenomenology constrains the scales: spontaneous CP violation and a new vector-like down quark mass follow from Nelson-Barr quality and missing baryon violation. It predicts a neutron decay into a charged kaon and a charged lepton, within reach of Hyper-Kamiokande, JUNO, and DUNE.
arxiv-2604-00266: Gürel and Gündüz study bi-amalgamated algebras, finding dimension and depth under fairly general settings. They derive exact Cohen-Macaulayness rules from maximal and big Cohen-Macaulay modules of the base ring. The Gorenstein property is pinned down through canonical modules of two rings. Their results build Gorenstein algebroid curves from amalgamated rings of both kinds, with a brief remark on the universally catenary property.
arxiv-2604-00366: Yoshida studies exceptional points, where eigenvalues and eigenvectors merge, in their multifold form. The doubling theorem for such points had only covered two-fold cases, even in the linear limit. He treats systems where nonlinearity enters through eigenvalues and introduces frequency-momentum winding numbers. These new invariants classify multifold points across the Brillouin zone for any fold count and band count. They give one proof of doubling with no symmetry and under several symmetry rules, including parity-time and charge-conjugation-parity rules.
arxiv-2604-00466: Douba and colleagues build reflection groups that are convex cocompact and hyperbolic, with limit sets in three dimensions. Any three-dimensional simplicial complex on n vertices feeds the construction, which returns a right-angled reflection group on real hyperbolic n-space. Its nerve is exactly the Przytycki-Świątkowski subdivision of the starting complex. The group also sits thinly inside an n-dimensional cocompact arithmetic hyperbolic lattice. The result settles Kapovich's question: such groups exist whose limit sets are Čech cohomology spheres other than the standard sphere.
arxiv-2604-00666: Chen and colleagues propose TRIMS, a path-guided fine-tuning framework for diffusion language models. Diffusion models promise low-latency generation through parallel output, but efficiency depends heavily on the decoding path. Standard training gives no explicit guidance over the order tokens are revealed, creating a train-inference mismatch and suboptimal output behaviour. TRIMS injects path supervision into masked training with minimal overhead. Instead of costly diffusion-based distillation, it uses light signals from an autoregressive teacher to guide path-aware masking.
arxiv-2604-00866: Okada, Sanyal, and Verma study long-lived heavy neutral leptons from decays of pair-produced neutrinophilic charged Higgs bosons into those leptons plus charged leptons. In this framework, sizable Dirac Yukawa couplings arise because the extra doublet's vacuum expectation value is small, even at a low seesaw scale. Simulations show one displaced vertex can reach high statistical significance for pair-production cross sections above order 1 femtobarn. Two displaced vertices stay challenging even at order 10 femtobarns.
arxiv-2604-01066: Espinal Maya splits human capital into bodily, routine, aided work. He builds a function where AI takes over for routine work and lifts aided work, deriving a Mincer wage formula. Using LLM-made gauges for items across 440 Colombian jobs and data on 105,517 workers, he fits the formula. Aided work returns rise with AI uptake in formal work, while off-books workers miss boosts, showing formal status drives it. The binding constraint in the Global South on human-AI teamwork is labor rules, not tech access.
arxiv-2604-01166: Greensite studies a quenched SU(2) by U(1) gauge Higgs theory on a lattice. It is coupled to a static vector-like fermion in the same representation as the Higgs field. He describes new kinds of locally gauge-invariant electrically charged and neutral states, orthogonal to constructions from decades ago. They differ in how dynamical fields dress the static source. The neutral fermion proves much lighter than any charged state. The charged spectrum holds at least two states of different mass.
arxiv-2604-01266: Polson, Sokolov, and Zantedeschi connect horseshoe prior theory to the moderate deviation principle. Carvalho's theorems give tight log bounds for marginal density near the origin and a super-efficient convergence rate for the Bayes density when sparse. The Shrink Globally, Act Locally paper set rules on prior behavior at the origin for sparsity adaptation. These results are finite early signs of the asymptotic moderate deviation principle. The log-pole singularity marks the origin integrability edge that selects the threshold, and tail strength above it shapes Bayes risk.
arxiv-2604-02266: Zheng and colleagues build a real time Zak-OTFS receiver on GPUs for high mobility wireless links. OTFS beats OFDM in fast channels but its delay Doppler form is costly, especially on large grids. Hardware algorithm co-design exploiting channel sparsity, compact matrix operations and a branchless equalizer cuts compute and memory sharply. The system meets real time deadlines and tops 900 Mbps on a large grid, scaling well across CPU and GPU platforms from Jetson Orin to H200.
arxiv-2604-02366: Parisel stress tests cloud access controls far outside their home domain. A sister paper proves a Burau Lyapunov exponent separates focused from dispersed ratchets in cloud graphs, and no abelian stat matches it. To test the claim beyond fake data, Parisel runs the same pipeline as is on solar fields, a system unrelated to cloud identity. Its eruptive or confined outcomes, known from decades of solar study, provide an independent check.
arxiv-2604-02466: Gimeno and Peterson study the effective stability of near-rectilinear halo orbits around the Earth-Moon L2 point, where bands of stable orbits sit inside strongly unstable regions. Using high-order Taylor expansions and discrete Nekhoroshev-type estimates, they map geometric stability limits into real spatial coordinates. For mission lifetimes of 10 to 50 years, the stable region is set by the analytic domain of the optimized normal form, not by slow exponential drift.
arxiv-2604-02766: Oh and five colleagues test active preference learning against random sampling for online direct preference optimization with modern language models. Uncertainty-based selection yields negligible gains in proxy win rates over random sampling across harmlessness, helpfulness, and instruction-following settings. Worse, win rates can rise while general capability falls, and active selection fails to prevent that collapse or cut variance much better than random sampling.
arxiv-2604-03266: Kaszyński shows in a 2026 study that teams of agents can invent compositional codes for hidden physical properties from frozen video features alone. Communicating through a narrow bottleneck with iterated learning, four agents converged on codes separating elasticity, friction, and mass ratio without labels. The learned code also supported planning and reached 85.6 percent mass-comparison accuracy on real camera footage.
arxiv-2604-03366: Di Marco offers a 2026 guide chapter to working with data from IXPE, the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer. The chapter introduces the spacecraft and instrument, then covers pulling polarimetric signals from data, tuning response, and dodging built-in errors in formats and processing. It sums up both model-free and model-based studies and the instrument response options, aiming to get the most scientific return from each pointing.
arxiv-2604-03466: Koots, Mirahmadi, and Pérez-Ríos overturn the age-old Lindemann-Hinshelwood picture for barrierless three-body reactions. Using standard paths in hyperspherical coordinates, they show direct three-body motion matches ion-atom merging rates across a wide temperature range, with no middle complexes or steady-state assumptions. The framework clears up theory-test gaps across air, plasma, and ultracold chemistry.
arxiv-2604-03566: Nguyen and Uribe study Fréchet regression. It models links between inputs and outputs on general metric spaces like chance spreads or positive matrices. They give a condition that guarantees a best fit exists and marks how far the fit can stretch beyond the data. Under that condition, the goal has no local peaks. They also build a proven projection-free algorithm for near-still points and a random rewrite for large-scale problems.
arxiv-2604-03766: Ranjeet Kumbhar and colleagues tested three controllers for a lower-limb exoskeleton helping wearers rise from sitting to standing. A CAD-based Simscape model supplied realistic hip, knee, and ankle tracks across three movement phases. Their hybrid PID-LQR blend cut tracking error by over 70 percent at hip and knee versus PID alone, slashed settling time, and kept overshoot small.
arxiv-2604-03966: Bilal Ahmad Rather studied the independent domination polynomial of comaximal graphs of commutative rings. In the comaximal graph, two distinct ring elements link when their generated ideals sum to the whole ring. The paper treats the polynomial for integers modulo n, covering unimodal and log-concave traits for certain n, plus zeros and bounds. It also determines the independence polynomial for special n and gives a general result tied to it.
arxiv-2604-04266: Beckers and Colombo control physical systems described by partial differential equations, where exact models are hard to obtain. Their method learns the unknown energy structure of a distributed port-Hamiltonian system from data, using Gaussian processes. The learned model's uncertainty feeds into an energy-based safety analysis, giving probabilistic guarantees that closed-loop paths stay bounded despite model errors. A simulated shallow water system shows the approach.
arxiv-2604-04466: Lachish and colleagues characterize one-sided error testable properties in bounded degeneracy graphs under the random neighbor oracle model. A tester explores a graph by sampling neighbors; a property is testable with one-sided error when query complexity stays size-independent. But broader p-degenerate graphs allow high-degree hubs hiding forbidden subgraphs from local search. The team characterizes all one-sided error testable properties in p-degenerate graphs. Testability turns on forbidden-structure connectivity: a property is testable exactly when violations cannot fragment across high-degree neighborhoods.
arxiv-2604-05066: Zhu and three co-authors present AutoLALA, an open tool that analyzes locality in affine loop programs. Data movement is the bottleneck in computing, and for loop programs in HPC and AI, moving data through memory often costs more than arithmetic. The tool accepts programs in a special language and lowers them to polyhedral sets and maps. It produces closed formulas for reuse distance and data movement complexity. AutoLALA implements locality analysis with the data movement distance framework for reasoning about memory costs.
arxiv-2604-05166: Rismani and four colleagues examine how users' mental models shape their use of AI writing aides. They contrast job models of what the system does with build models of how it works, testing acts: asking, taking, or editing tips. People were primed with varied texts before writing a letter with an aide that sometimes offered bad-grammar tips, testing watch. Build-model people grasped the system better and judged it more usable, yet made more grammar errors, showing knowing and trust can backfire when watch is needed.
arxiv-2604-05366: Lee shows that shrinking 3D reconstruction models needs no per-scene training at all, overturning the assumption behind every current compressor. Because the bulky parameter vectors sit in a middling dimension range, one random rotation reshapes any input so its coordinates follow a predictable Beta law. That makes a precomputed, data-free quantizer nearly optimal, under three times the theoretical floor. His method also predicts in advance which parameters can shrink and by how much, and it compresses one splatting model more than threefold with tiny rendering loss.
arxiv-2604-06066: In a 2026 study, Zhou asks whether Outlines decoding alone can stop language models snowballing early errors during free-text self-correction. The target failure is hallucination snowballing, where a model keeps backing early errors. Testing Qwen3-8B, an 8-billion-parameter model, he finds set format rules do not improve self-correction. Instead they trigger structure snowballing, a new failure mode where format rules trap the model. The agent nails surface syntax yet misses deeper meaning errors. Zhou calls the tradeoff an alignment tax.
arxiv-2604-06366: Corlouer, Semler, Strang, and Gietelink Oldenziel study stochastic gradient descent in deep linear networks. Gradient descent shows saddle-to-saddle dynamics, but noise effects stay poorly known. They model training as Langevin motion with changing noise. With aligned and even weights, they split motion into per-mode rules. Maximal diffusion leads full learning. Per mode, the stationary distribution matches gradient flow without label noise, and nears a Boltzmann distribution with label noise. Tests confirm the theory without them. Noise thus encodes feature-learning progress without changing saddle-to-saddle dynamics.
arxiv-2604-06866: Khatun, Karim, and Usman build a lean quantum residual neural network that needs no post-selection. Residual links run through a set mixture of identity steps and variational unitaries, keeping training fully differentiable. Unlike prior designs, the network skips that step while keeping residual learning, and flags circuit builds that may soften barren plateaus. On MNIST, CIFAR, and SARFish image tasks it reaches 99 percent binary and 80 percent multi-class accuracy, matching standard models with 10 times fewer gates, plus adversarial robustness.
arxiv-2604-06966: Ma and eight colleagues steady reward learning for masked step-by-step images with MAR-GRPO. Taking it to hybrid step-by-step-diffusion models is hard because mixed use and chance guesses shake it. The noise head drives noisy gradients, causing shakes and early stalls. Their fix means over noise paths to set the update way. It tunes only the most unsure tokens and filters out step tokens that miss the output. Tests show gains in quality, training calm, and spatial structure over base and pre-learning models.
arxiv-2604-07066: Yu and sixteen colleagues present a shared task that scores feeling in text along two sliding scales, pleasantness and energy, rather than plain good or bad tags. The task, called DimABSA, moves past shop reviews to public topics like politics, energy, and climate, and adds a stance track that treats stance aims as aspects. Track one asks for aspect feeling scores, triples, and four part extracts, while track two asks for stance scores alone. More than four hundred teams joined, with over one hundred final entries.
arxiv-2604-07366: Dai and three colleagues say learned PDE solvers need a fresh core idea: track how uncertainty moves, not just guess states.
